title: Development of a predictive model for the risk of microalbuminuria: comparison of 2 machine learning algorithms.
summary: A Random Forest model using nine clinical variables predicted MAU among 981 hospitalized T2DM patients (test AUC 0.87); SHAP associated HbA1c, NLR and 25(OH)D with risk. This is a single-center retrospective prediction, not evidence of clinical benefit.
ai_technology: logistic screening selects nine variables, then Random Forest and BP neural-network models predict MAU; SHAP interprets RF feature contributions.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: retrospective data from 981 hospitalized T2DM patients (333 MAU) produced an RF risk model with reported test AUC 0.87 and associations for HbA1c, NLR and 25(OH)D.
evidence.unknown: Methods: random 70/30 training/test split, SMOTE applied to training data, and five-fold cross-validation. Validation is internal and single-center; it does not establish clinical benefit or external performance.
evidence.ai_role: logistic screening selects nine variables, then Random Forest and BP neural-network models predict MAU; SHAP interprets RF feature contributions.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
